title: Zero-section integration under Cartesian bundle change
statement: In [def-pur-conventions], let B and B′ be Noetherian finite-type k-schemes, F and F′ rank-d finite locally free modules, and v:E(F′)→E(F) over b:B′→B a Cartesian projection square preserving zero. The pullback of the actual vectorBetaInverse of [def-pur-orientation-refinement-comparisons], followed by the specified section exchange, equals the actual base Tate comparison followed by vectorBetaInverse for F′. No linearity of v is imposed. The coefficient exponent is the fixed diagonal exponent, at every positive coefficient level.

source.place: Compatibility paragraph: base change of the normalized trace and transposition; zero-section normalization of the vector-purity proposition.

proof.text: Apply the compact-support normalized trace equation to the given zero-preserving Cartesian presentation. Transpose using the actual two Brown adjunctions. The private integration_mate_square proves this step directly from mateEquiv_counit, counit naturality, exchange naturality and the adjunction Hom bijections; no purity family or assumed orientation is substituted.

source.place: Compatibility paragraph: base change of the normalized trace and transposition; zero-section normalization of the vector-purity proposition.

proof.text: Pull the obtained total-space orientation square along the new zero section. Naturality of the pullback compositor moves the old orientation across the section square. The ordered Tate coefficient square identifies the remaining source factors with base Tate pullback followed by inverse new zero-section Tate comparison. The private restrict_orientation_square performs these compositions. Finally adjunction naturality on the source identifies both normalized adjuncts with the defining vectorBetaInverse. Rank zero and empty bases require no case distinction.
